title: A Study in Healthy Participants to Test How Well Different Doses of SIM0709 Are Tolerated
official: A Phase I Single-blind, Randomised, Placebo-controlled Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Single and Multiple Rising Doses of SIM0709 in Healthy Participants
summary: This trial initiates the clinical development of SIM0709. Effects of single and multiple rising doses of SIM0709 on safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity and pharmacodynamics will be assessed.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Healthy male or female trial participant according to the assessment of the investigator, as based on a complete medical history including a physical examination, vital signs (BP, PR, BT), 12-lead ECG, and clinical laboratory tests
2. Age of 18 to 55 years (inclusive)
3. BMI of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2 (inclusive)
4. Signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with ICH-GCP and local legislation prior to admission to the trial
5. Female trial participants must be of non-childbearing potential, defined as meeting at least one of the following criteria

   1. Permanent sterilisation: Documented evidence or a medical history considered reliable by the investigator, confirming permanent sterilisation, including hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy, or bilateral oophorectomy.
   2. Postmenopausal state: Defined as amenorrhea (no menses) for at least 12 months without an alternative medical cause. For all such participants, postmenopausal status must be confirmed at screening by a follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level \> 40 U/L and estradiol \< 30 ng/L. (Female participants receiving hormone replacement therapy are excluded from this postmenopausal definition unless they meet the criteria for permanent sterilisation as specified in Criterion 5a).
6. From screening until 30 days after trial completion, male participants must use a condom during sexual intercourse with a WOCBP partner and refrain from donating sperm.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any finding in the medical examination (including BP, PR, temperature or ECG) deviating from normal and assessed as clinically relevant by the investigator
2. Repeated measurement of systolic blood pressure outside the range of 90 to 140 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure outside the range of 50 to 90 mmHg, or repeated pulse rate outside the range of 50 to 100 bpm
3. Any laboratory value outside the reference range that the investigator considers to be of clinical relevance. For key liver and renal parameters, participants must be excluded if they meet any of the following criteria upon repeated testing:

   1. ALT or AST \> 1.5 × ULN (Upper Limit of Normal)
   2. Total Bilirubin \> 1.5 × ULN
   3. Creatinine \> 1.5 × ULN or eGFR \< 80 mL/min/1.73 m²
4. Any clinically relevant concomitant disease or chronic disorder (including but not limited to gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders) that, in the judgment of the investigator, compromises participant safety or interferes with the study evaluations
5. Diseases of the central nervous system (including but not limited to any kind of seizures or stroke), and other relevant neurological or psychiatric disorders
6. History of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts
7. Relevant chronic or acute infections, including but not limited to:

   1. Hepatitis B (HBV) infection, as evidenced by confirmed positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Participants with a positive hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) must be excluded unless a follow-up HBV DNA PCR test is negative and there is no evidence of active HBV infection
   2. Hepatitis C (HCV) infection, as confirmed by positive anti-HCV antibodies
   3. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections, as confirmed by an appropriate confirmatory test
8. Active or latent tuberculosis (TB), Latent TB is determined by a positive GRA such as QuantiFERON®-TB-Gold Plus or T-spot at screening (an indeterminate result can be repeated once; a confirmed indeterminate result is also exclusionary)
